Subject: Request: sub-50ms p95 SLA for Aurora real-time inference

Jordan —

Thanks again for last week’s demo. We ran a short internal spike with the test model and the results are encouraging, but Aurora has a hard product requirement: the inference path for our customer-facing chat and intent routing needs to meet p95 <= 50ms in our US West region for requests under 128 tokens. This is a gating item for our pilot.

Can Redwood provide a carveout SLA (including operational runbook and escalation path) to commit to 50ms p95 for a scoped workload (initially ~150 RPS peak, ~60M requests/month) for a 12-month term? If that requires reserved capacity / dedicated pool, please outline the minimum commitment and cost delta.

We'd like to move quickly — is there a technical/contractual path to make this happen?

— Lena
Head of Product Operations, Aurora Corp

Subject: RE: Fwd: Request: sub-50ms p95 SLA for Aurora real-time inference

Jordan / team —

Technical readout after reviewing the sample traffic:
- Feasibility: Achievable with constraints. For sub-50ms p95 we should run Aurora on a dedicated pool using a smaller quantized model plus aggressive prefix/KV caching. Recommended config: dedicated pool of 4xA10x or 2xA100 (depending on provisioning), model variant: redwood-lite-v2-8q, quantization+operator kernels tuned for 128-token requests.
- Warm-up: Cold-starts and cache-warming will cause higher tail latency for the first ~30–90s after a scale event. We can mitigate with pre-warm hooks and a short traffic ramp.
- Fallbacks: Provide automatic fallback to redwood-mini-4q (higher latency, lower cost) with explicit SLA clauses for fallback windows. Suggest p95 target: 50ms for steady-state, allow p95 <= 70ms during controlled burst/startup windows and p99 <= 200ms for rare escalations.
- Monitoring: Need transaction-level tracing (sampled), token-level cost telemetry, and synthetic checks from us-west. We can expose runbook links and traces in the Console.

Operation / Cost estimate (very rough):
- Dedicated pool (4xA10x): ~$65k/month gross cost; pass-through pricing + 20% margin -> list ~78k/month. If they want guaranteed <50ms at 150 RPS sustained, recommend 12-month commit.
- Pilot: 30-day pilot with pre-warm + load tests to validate the config; pilot cost estimated ~30k (setup + reserved capacity pro-rated).

Risk notes:
- If Aurora spikes >>150 RPS we must have clear contractual burst policy (burst queueing or auto-burst to shared infra with laxed SLA).
- Model regression risk: quantized model must be validated on Aurora prompts — recommend acceptance tests before go-live.

I can draft the technical appendix for the SLA addendum (ops/runbook, warm-up behavior, synthetic checks). Need Legal to review liability language for fallback windows.

— Grace
Director, Product — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: draft-sla-technical-appendix.md (will add to Drive)
